analysis.investment_thesis: Delhivery's Magic Formula metrics are near-zero — earnings yield of ~1% (EBIT INR 376 Cr / EV ~INR 35,762 Cr) and ROCE of just 2.47% — making it uninvestable under my framework. The company only generated its first positive net profit (INR 162 Cr) in FY25 after years of cumulative losses exceeding INR 4,500 Cr.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 32.5% over 6 years is impressive and shows genuine scale capture in India's e-commerce logistics market
OCF turned firmly positive in FY24–25 (INR 472–567 Cr), and FCF is barely positive (INR 92 Cr in FY25), suggesting the inflection has begun
No promoter overhang; strong institutional support (FII 48.57% + DII 34.98%) signals sophisticated investor confidence in the long-term thesis
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~1% is catastrophically below Magic Formula minimums — at Market Cap INR 34,676 Cr on EBIT of INR 376 Cr, the stock needs to grow earnings ~10-12x just to be fairly valued by my standards
ROCE of 2.47% means the business is currently destroying economic value relative to cost of capital — logistics is inherently capital-intensive with razor-thin margins
Finance costs of INR 126 Cr consuming one-third of EBIT; P/E of 192x means any operational stumble causes severe multiple compression
red_flags: Cumulative net losses from FY19–FY24 exceed INR 4,500 Cr — the Magic Formula literally cannot compute for most of this company's history because EBIT was negative
Other Income (INR 442 Cr in FY25) — mainly interest on cash — is nearly as large as operating income (INR 376 Cr); the core logistics business barely earns its keep
No promoter holding at all — ownership structure is entirely institutional, creating governance questions and potential volatility risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict is swift: EV ≈ INR 35,762 Cr, EBIT = INR 376 Cr, Earnings Yield = 1.05%. ROCE = 2.47%. Both metrics are in the bottom decile of any screen I would run. My framework requires positive EBIT sustained over time — Delhivery only achieved this in FY24 for the first time. The business model (asset-light logistics network) has theoretical merit, but 'theoretical merit' is not a Magic Formula input.

Investors here are buying a story about scale economics and margin expansion to 5–8% operating margins. That may happen, but I pay for demonstrated earnings power, not projections. At INR 34,676 Cr market cap on INR 162 Cr net profit, you need everything to go right for a decade before this stock earns its valuation. That's speculation, not value investing.
